meta.title: Next Session — Candidate Scenes
meta.subtitle: The GM's working slate for the session after Summer 1224 (next play: the 22nd). Wilhelm is bound for Scarem Montem; the northern party owes a return to Tormente and means to enter the Carnac regio. Played scenes from the 2026-08-08 session are marked and now live in the Chronicle. Derived from the Open Questions prep hub (q027).
meta.source: open_questions.json → q027 "What are we preparing for next session?" (+ the Rody hand-off, t023/q026)
meta.status_note: Developed = prepped and ready to stage · Deferred = deliberately left to improvise · Needs prep = flagged but not yet developed · Played = staged in the 2026-08-08 session (see the Chronicle)

scenes.title: What Wilhelm's assistants bring back — and can it break the thesis?
scenes.hook: Wilhelm's research assistants return from the winter gathering (sent west and south, paid in grain and silver). The live beat is whether any of it FALSIFIES the folk-magic thesis rather than confirming it.
scenes.detail: ADVANCED (Summer 1224): Carl & Isaac returned — the technique worked but the madness cost was realized (a suicide and a double killing among ~12-15 students); the temporal mage's brass ACORN turned up with no magic residue. The weak maritime citation is still unfilled, and still gates the delivery (s6). A negative result — a tradition that works without leaning on the environment, or the missing open-ocean storm-prediction / current-finding citation turning out not to exist — forces Wilhelm to revise before he can deliver to Scarem Montem (see s6). Developed: the negation is a MADNESS failure rate that breaks the scalable / vis-factory case without disproving the magic itself; the assistants also flag a temporal hedge mage who beat the Limit of Time, leaving Wilhelm an origin-less brass egg.

scenes.title: Where does Foxglove get off the ship?
scenes.hook: Foxglove is aboard the Tide of Memory with roughly five bags of stolen Roman dragon-gold — lifted the same night Dagmar agreed to run Tormente's peace-errand. She has every reason to vanish with the hoard before the theft surfaces, and the ship is already running north toward a Stonehenge-Tribunal port.
scenes.detail: PLAYED (Summer 1224): in London the gold proved unspendable in a silver economy; Foxglove fenced only three coins at a brutal one-for-one and kept the bulk, staying with the covenant for cover (she is also wanted elsewhere) — Where she gets off (and whether she deserts outright), and the fallout if she is still aboard when Dagmar returns to Tormente and the missing hoard is noticed, are player calls. What got prepped is the WORLD constraint: a GM reference on converting Roman gold c.1224 — no gold coinage on a silver standard, so bullion by weight only (melt, goldsmiths, moneylenders, Flanders/Lombard bankers, worked goods, the Church), plus treasure-trove and provenance friction and no collector market yet.

scenes.title: Does Valdemar join Dagmar for the dragon leg?
scenes.hook: The northbound errand — carry the jewelled crown to Tormente's estranged kin off Scarborough / Newcastle — is a two-magus job. Valdemar (no familiar yet, and tied to the sea-fae Rán) is a natural companion for dragon diplomacy against a wyrm claiming Norse descent.
scenes.detail: PLAYED (Summer 1224): Valdemar joined — the Tide met his ship off Northumbria and he sailed on for the dragon leg — Dagmar has already invited Llewellyn ex Miscellanea by Redcap. Deferred: Valdemar's player has been absent, so the GM will improvise whether he signs on rather than pre-stage it. His Rán connection is worth watching against the kin-dragon's claim (s4).

scenes.title: The kin-dragon claims descent from Jörmungandr — the Mímormr reveal
scenes.hook: The reveal behind the errand: the estranged dragon claims descent from Jörmungandr, the Midgard Serpent, styling itself the greatest magical being that ever was. For a Norse-seiðr saga this is a cosmological escalation.
scenes.detail: PLAYED (Summer 1224): the worm is Mímormr, self-proclaimed great-grandchild of Jörmungandr; delivering Tormente's crown FREED it (a name-release), and it is now loosed toward the North Sea. The sequel is s8 — Developed: the claim is FALSE but sincerely believed by Mímormr, a cursed bone-speaking scholar-wyrm. Tormente (a trickster) is using Dagmar to break Mímormr's curse — and freeing it looses a regional threat. Full build in t072; recontextualizes the Carnac regio's guardianship and frames Tormente's magnitude-10 Might as merely the lesser sibling's.

scenes.title: Éogan and the capricorn
scenes.hook: On the voyage home from Ireland a Magic-realm capricorn (sea-goat) singles Éogan out and paces his ship — offered as his first familiar prospect. The work is courting it and the binding lab-work, not an instant bond.
scenes.detail: ADVANCED (Spring 1224): Éogan spotted the capricorn at a river-mouth near Drogheda (it favours salt-meets-fresh water), took a water sample and cast a relocation spell. Courtship and binding are still ahead. Developed: the draw is independent of the 'small fae drawn to Éogan/Stijntje' affinity; its signature specialty is CROSSING THRESHOLDS INTO REGIONES (mythic grounding in Enki's Goat-Fish and Macrobius's Gate of the Gods). Corpus build/bind references and a suggested Might ~12–16 Magic build are recorded. What it wants in exchange remains open.

scenes.title: Does Wilhelm sail to Scarem Montem? — and the three sealed chests
scenes.hook: The ship-for-book swap is in motion — the Hound of Cassel is under Wilhelm's control and headed back to Scarem Montem, and what he owes them is the folk-magic thesis. Whether he arrives with a finished thesis or one still short its maritime example hinges on s1.
scenes.detail: SET UP (Summer 1224): Wilhelm now has the Hound of Cassel and found the three sealed chests aboard (held from the Scarem Montem raid; still unopened, boat warded). The delivery is next session's anchor. Developed: the three sealed chests aboard the Hound of Cassel are intercepted Bishopric-of-Liège ↔ Scarem Montem cipher letters exposing a Church/State suborning — a Code violation tied to the Brabant conspiracy. Ring-based public/private-key crypto lets the covenant PROVE the correspondents but mostly not read the content. Wilhelm may be carrying Scarem Montem's own incriminating mail back to them: return it, keep it, or weaponise it in the swap? The Hound itself is warded with a 1-month-duration ward against scrying, cast by Wilhelm, for the run to Scarem Montem.

scenes.title: The Rody hand-off at Cruachan
scenes.hook: The Connacht → Hermetic delivery custom passed the party a Fae changeling — Rody — as an 'owed' Gifted-child delivery, while a real Gifted child is still missing, taken by the Fae. The party chose not to interrogate or trade with the changeling directly.
scenes.detail: PLAYED (Summer 1224): delivered. Rody (confirmed fully Fae) was left with the Cruachan magi Gráinne & Tadhg; the real child is still missing — Their plan was to quietly brief the receiving Hermetic magi near the Hill of Uisneach once the delivery completes. The open beats: does that briefing actually happen on the way home, and how did a Fae changeling come to be treated as a Gifted-child delivery in the first place? Flagged as a live thread but not yet developed.

scenes.title: Return to Tormente — with Mímormr's token
scenes.thread: The dragon errand / the Carnac regio
scenes.hook: Dagmar carries Mímormr's token back to Tormente, expecting passage into the Carnac regio — but Tormente sent him to free a prisoner it had bound, and may not deal straight.
scenes.detail: Tormente framed itself as 'estranged kin' and used Dagmar to break Mímormr's binding. What Tormente actually wanted, whether it honours the regio bargain, and how it reacts to Mímormr's freedom (and the stolen five bags of gold, if noticed) are all live. Flagged for the 22nd as the return to the first dragon.

scenes.title: Into the magical regio — and Llewellyn's gambit
scenes.hook: Once Tormente grants passage, the party enters the Aquam-tinged Carnac regio — where Llewellyn hopes the irregular time-flow will let him safely unwind his Zeno's-paradox longevity working.
scenes.detail: Llewellyn wants to 'catch the tide going out' — end his half-life-forever working in a place where time runs irregular, ideally with backup, before a sudden failure turns catastrophic. His found time-quartz crystal reads the flows. What the regio holds, and whether the gambit works, is the payoff.

scenes.title: The regiones behind Tormente
scenes.thread: The dragon errand / the Carnac regio
scenes.hook: The next-session objective for the northern party: reach the regiones gated behind Tormente — more than one lies back there.
scenes.detail: Umbrella objective for the 22nd. Beyond Tormente's ground sits a cluster of regiones — the Aquam-tinged Carnac regio (s9) and whatever else the dragon conceals. Runs straight off s8 (the return with Mímormr's token) and into s9 (Llewellyn's time-flow gambit inside the regio).
